goal: Determine the smallest source-bound learning graph that can help a user understand ontology concepts, expose what they do not understand, formulate a better next question, and choose but not execute the next governed route. Produce an exact-bound candidate node/relation model and a detailed introductory guide grounded primarily in the DomainSpec implementation-conformance ontology JSON and HTML, with current cyberAlchemy-v2 ontology experiments used as owned precedents and boundary evidence.
context: The primary candidate ontology defines architecture concept types, properties, relations, constraints, profiles, observations, and explainable findings with authority_effect none; its HTML already supports search, lenses, inspection, and a beginner guide. Current cyberAlchemy-v2 work includes an Interactive Ontology Learning Map, ontology candidate graph, several ontology evidence-workbench experiments, and related authority-safe read models, so this research must distinguish composition from duplication. The result is private, candidate-local research: it may recommend node and relation candidates and a next-route UX, but it cannot mutate ontology, canonical definitions, existing HTML, product code, Inventory, dispatch ledger, publication, release, or authority state.
anti_bias_global: Source-grounded composition versus learner-centered invention under explicit ontology, evidence, comprehension, and governance boundaries.

groups.anti_bias: Composite source-corpus and methodology axis: primary executable DomainSpec experiment, cross-experiment governance and runtime precedents, and learner-centered human-view evidence.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs exact JSON, HTML, profile, fixture, and validator anatomy on the primary DomainSpec experiment while agent 1 runs a cross-experiment owner, contract, and proof-ceiling survey on the source-corpus and methodology axes; a bias in agent 0 toward generalizing one experiment would be exposed by agent 1's overlapping or superseding owners, while a bias in agent 1 toward broad reuse would be exposed by agent 0's exact primary schema and runtime constraints.

Agent 0 runs machine-contract and implemented-view analysis while agent 2 runs learner-journey, question-formation, confusion, and comprehension analysis on the methodology axis; a bias in agent 0 toward equating inspectability with learning would be exposed by agent 2's human-evidence boundary, while a bias in agent 2 toward unconstrained pedagogy would be exposed by agent 0's typed source and owner bindings.

Agent 1 runs ontology-lifecycle, candidate-graph, workbench, and governed-route precedent analysis while agent 2 runs novice comprehension and question-to-route affordance analysis on the source-corpus and methodology axes; a bias in agent 1 toward governance-first complexity would be exposed by agent 2's smallest learner job, while a bias in agent 2 toward a new learner model would be exposed by agent 1's existing IOLM, Way Clear, and projection owners.

groups.anti_bias: Attack-vector axis: precedent ownership, non-vacuity witness, and definitional plus scope non-collapse.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs the precedent and owner gate while agent 1 runs finite learner-witness and abstention pressure on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward declaring the idea already owned would be exposed by agent 1 when existing components cannot produce a discriminating learner outcome, while a bias in agent 1 toward new machinery would be exposed by agent 0 when IOLM, Way Clear, the primary guide, or workbench already owns it.

Agent 0 runs ownership and duplication classification while agent 2 runs definitional and scope-collapse attacks on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward extending one broad ontology owner would be exposed by agent 2 when learner state, workflow state, and semantic meaning collapse, while a bias in agent 2 toward proliferating terms would be exposed by agent 0 when an existing projection or relation already owns the distinction.

Agent 1 runs concrete positive, confusion, unknown, and abstention witnesses while agent 2 runs tautology, category-error, and authority-collapse attacks on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 1 toward a persuasive demo would be exposed by agent 2 when a node merely renames UI state, while a bias in agent 2 toward semantic purity would be exposed by agent 1 when a distinct relation changes the next question or route verdict observably.

agents.angle: Precedent gate: verify whether each proposed node, relation, projection, learner loop, and next-route contract is already owned, build-from-owned, or genuinely unowned.

Build the smallest paper-executable fixture around architecture.RuleImplementation, at least one property/profile expectation, one observed fact, one finding, one source-backed explanation, one learner confusion, one better next question, one unknown/residue, and one candidate governed route. agents.angle: Definitional and scope gate: attack collapse among source meaning, ontology concept, evidence, learner state, confusion, question, unknown, workflow, route suggestion, approval, and authority.

Test whether LearningGraph is a real projection/query model or a renamed graph UI; whether QuestionNode and UnknownNode are durable semantic objects, ephemeral learner/session state, or ordinary evidence residue; whether understands, confused_about, asks_next, explains, evidenced_by, blocks, and routes_to have distinct endpoints and failure modes; and whether a candidate route recommendation remains separate from confirmation, dispatch, execution, promotion, and authority. Return KEEP/MERGE/RENAME/DEFER/KILL with exact citations and a smallest repaired vocabulary. KILL only tautological or definitionally collapsed candidates.

Write findings.md only from the evidence-closed synthesis and reviewer receipts. Use /home/vrondelli/projects/domainspec-core/.agents/skills/whisper/SKILL.md with the product_research_blueprint preset.
